title.narrative: Independent Feedback, Operational Reviews and Monitoring (I-FORM) of AAWAZ-II Programme (Pakistan)

description.narrative:
OPM was the third-party evaluator of the FCDO-funded Aawaz II (voice and accountability) programme in two major provinces of Pakistan, i.e., Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP). The Aawaz II programme aimed to increase voice, choice & control for women, girls, boys, youth, religious minorities & marginalised groups; protect them from exploitation; and prevent discrimination & intolerance. The programme prioritised: child labour; child & forced marriages; Gender-based Violence (GBV); and discrimination & intolerance to which marginalised groups are extremely vulnerable. Intermediate programme outcomes focused on the strengthening government institutions through effective laws & policies; and improving social attitudes to prevent abuse and intolerance. These changes were supported by outputs, such as enhanced legislative frameworks, protection systems, and community actions to prevent conflict & promote tolerance.
OPM’s major independent evaluation work included: carrying out operational reviews, spot checks, and beneficiary feedback on the selected themes of Inclusion and Gender-based Violence, employing qualitative and quantitative data collection approaches and tools. In addition, OPM also provided coordination and documentation support for the Quarterly Technical Reviews (QTRs), aggregation of data on results and Value for Money (VfM) analysis from implementing partners, and facilitation of learning across the Aawaz II programme. The key principles of OPM’s approach to this assignment were participation, learning & sharing, reliability, flexibility, inclusivity, and ensuring VfM. The nested logframe was also reviewed and updated during the project cycle. The Aawaz II dashboard was also maintained by OPM for tracking progress, collating and disseminating project-related information, and record keeping of all important documents.
